text:
Jules: Quick ask — we need a single-page, customer-facing flyer to send after next week's webinar. Audience: SREs / Platform & security buyers. Focus: deploy-mode tradeoffs (Hosted / Dedicated / Private), high-level SLA/security bullets, and two tiny benchmark callouts for latency and cost economics. Keep it non-technical, one column, with a clear CTA to book an eval.
Sasha: Got it. I can draft a clean one-pager. Do we want a visual decision strip (3 boxes) + a short comparison table? :thinking_face:
Ravi: Yes to the 3-box approach. Make the table tiny — 3 rows (Security, SLA, Typical buyer). For benchmarks: avoid raw, unverified numbers. Suggest phrasing like "industry-leading p95 latency" and "up to 3x cost savings with batching & quantization" — we can link to the benchmark page for details.
Jules: Good call on phrasing. Marketing should not publish exact latency without a reference. If we include a benchmark snippet, link it to the public benchmark doc and add a parenthetical: (tested on X hardware, workload specific).
Sasha: Draft outline I was thinking:
- Header: "Secure, predictable inference — pick the right deployment mode"
- 3 boxes: Hosted / Dedicated / Private (1 sentence benefit each)
- Tiny 3-row table comparing Security, SLA, Cost predictability
- Callouts: "When to choose" short bullets for each box
- Footer: CTA button text: `Book a deployment review` + short link to scheduling page
Ravi: For messaging: Hosted = fastest time-to-value, good for prototyping and SaaS; Dedicated = reserved GPU pools, SLA-backed latency/throughput; Private = VPC/on-prem for regulated data & KMS integrations. Keep it buyer-centric not product-heavy.
Ava: A couple security notes: 1) Don't promise specific cryptography or KMS partners unless cleared. 2) Remove any definitive claim about "air-gapped on-prem" unless ops has a validated package. 3) Include one line: "Compliance & controls: customizable networking, KMS integrations, and audit logging" — that's safe.
Jules: Thanks. Sasha, can you draft with those constraints and share the verbiage in this thread for quick review? Target: final design by EOD Friday for webinar follow-up email.
Sasha: On it. Quick copy draft below — please reply with edits.

```
Secure, predictable inference — pick the right deployment mode

Hosted · Fastest time-to-value for product teams. Redwood-hosted models, streaming responses, and starter quotas to get you to production quickly.

Dedicated · Predictable throughput & SLAs. Reserved GPU pools, configurable autoscale, and SLA-backed latency targets for steady production workloads.

Private · Compliance-first deployments. Customer-managed VPC and on-prem options with audit logs and KMS integrations.

At a glance (Security | SLA | Typical buyer):
- Hosted: Shared infra, standard access controls | Best-effort latency | Early-stage teams, product experiments
- Dedicated: Data-isolated pools, baseline controls | SLA-backed throughput & latency | Scale-up product teams, mid-market
- Private: Full network control, enterprise controls | Configurable SLAs | Regulated, security-sensitive enterprises

Why customers choose Redwood: industry-leading p95 latency (see benchmark) · Up to 3x unit-cost reduction with batching & quantization (workload dependent)

Ready to evaluate? Book a deployment review: https://redwood.ai/book-demo
```
Ravi: This is a solid first pass. Change one line: "industry-leading p95 latency (see benchmark)" -> "refer to our benchmark report for latency profiles by model and region" — less marketing-y but safer. Also please add a tiny legal footnote: "Performance varies by model, hardware, and prompt patterns."
Ava: Approved with those edits. Also remove the direct scheduling link in the public one-pager PDF — use a short link that lands on gated scheduling (leads) so we can route inbound appropriately.
Security-Bot: Reminder: any outbound claims referencing benchmarks must include a link to the canonical benchmark doc stored in Marketing Drive and a sign-off from Ops. Add `@ops` review step before publish.
Sasha: Will update copy and replace link with short gated link. I'll add the legal footnote and tag Ops for sign-off. Will post a PDF draft in this thread by tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
Jules: Perfect. Owner: Sasha. Reviewers: @Ravi, @Ava, @ops. Timeline: draft tomorrow AM, final by EOD Friday. Thanks everyone!
